learningObjective: Reclassify familiar interview rounds as overlapping evidence for five cross-cutting senior Applied Scientist signals, then prepare directly for the signal each prompt can reveal.
mediumRationale: Five compact semantic evidence cards are the smallest useful spatial explanation because the lesson is a reclassification, not a process: each stable signal appears as a heading, the card names multiple rounds where it can surface, and one targeted preparation drill follows.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected: a many-to-many graph between round types and five signals would create crossing edges and imply a fixed interview-loop topology that varies by employer.
mediumComparison.svg: Rejected: no quantitative scale, geometry, or fixed coordinates carry the lesson, and text in SVG would wrap less reliably at 390 CSS pixels.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Selected: directly labelled cards preserve the five-part grouping, expose overlap through explicit Seen in lines, remain native text for assistive technology, and reflow from two columns to one using the established responsive primitive.
mediumComparison.interaction: Rejected: filtering by round would hide the central fact that one prompt can produce evidence for several signals and would add state without new explanatory value.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected: the authoritative sources describe competency-based and Applied Scientist interviewing but do not provide a figure for this article's original five-signal synthesis. Public access was not treated as permission to copy any source artwork or arrangement.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected: the prose explains each signal and later lists preparation drills, but readers must mentally connect those signals across the conventional round labels. The grouped cards make that cross-cutting reclassification explicit at a glance.

pages.insight: The ML Design divider and timing strip introduce a conventional round label, beginning the closest technical-interview neighborhood.
The ML design overview combines vague product prompts, algorithm choice, trade-offs, and feature selection, showing that one nominal round can elicit both scoping and scientific reasoning.
The production checklist covers customer goals, global rollout, tooling, and training data, supplying concrete shipping evidence inside a technical design discussion.
The worked feed example explicitly reserves time for clarifying ambiguous requirements and then probes training and live data, directly supporting the article's scope-before-solve signal.
The neighboring worked-example page asks for algorithm trade-offs, a hypothesis, and offline and online evaluation, joining scientific understanding to production judgment.

The serving slide asks about model gates, monitoring, user feedback, updates, low-confidence behavior, latency, memory, compute, privacy, and interpretability—the article's boring middle of shipped ML.
The adjacent Rules of ML Engineering summary emphasizes observable metrics, launch discipline, error analysis, and training-serving skew before the deck changes to algorithms and data structures.
The Behavioral/Culture Interview divider begins a separate conventional round neighborhood with no claim that behavioral evidence is isolated from technical rounds.
The resource slide lists behavioral and general interview references but supplies no model connecting behavioral prompts to technical-round evidence.
The Leadership divider introduces the neighboring communication material.

The leadership slide recommends facts-first dialogue, examining one's own role, replacing either-or framing, keeping others safe, and speaking with confidence and humility; this closely matches constructive disagreement and low-ego collaboration.
The following DL Frameworks divider ends the behavioral and leadership neighborhood, confirming that the deck keeps these topics spatially separate from its ML design material.

deckReview.notes: GitHub Copilot CLI agent-2 (GPT-5.6 Sol) text-indexed all 214 physical PDF pages for interview, design, ambiguity, requirements, production, launch, behavioral, culture, leadership, disagreement, and communication concepts. Pages 159-170 and 207-211 were read as the complete matching neighborhoods, including their boundary slides. The deck supplies relevant examples on pages 161-164, 168-169, and 210, but it does not provide the article's five-signal taxonomy or show that conventional rounds collect overlapping evidence. No deck screenshot, wording, layout, or artwork is reused.

sources.title: Applied Scientist Interview Prep
sources.usage: Used as official employer guidance to verify that Applied Scientist loops assess technical and non-technical competencies, combine behavioral and technical questions, and cover problem solving and coding, knowledge depth and breadth, and Leadership Principles across assigned interviewers.
sources.license: Amazon publishes the page for candidate guidance but provides no clear permissive license for its text, videos, or artwork. No wording, media, page structure, or visual arrangement is copied; it is cited only to check the cross-competency premise.

sources.title: Structured Interviews
sources.usage: Used as authoritative U.S. government guidance to verify that structured interviews measure job-related competencies through past behavior and hypothetical situations and can assess interpersonal skills that other methods struggle to measure.
sources.license: As an official U.S. federal government resource, unmarked agency-authored material is generally not protected by U.S. copyright under 17 U.S.C. 105, subject to third-party exceptions. No text, form, or figure is reproduced.

sources.title: A Review of Structure in the Selection Interview
sources.usage: Used as a peer-reviewed primary review to check the role of job analysis, job-related questions, standardized evaluation, interviewer training, and multiple dimensions in making selection interviews more reliable and valid.
sources.license: The Personnel Psychology article is copyrighted by its publisher, and no open figure-reuse license was identified. No prose, data, table, figure, or visual structure is reused.

sourceReview.notes: The hardest prose-only mental model is that round names are containers, not the latent criteria. A system-design prompt can reveal scoping, science, shipping, and communication; a project-depth prompt can reveal shipping, science, disagreement handling, and room presence. The five signals and their preparation drills are the article author's synthesis rather than an empirically exhaustive or employer-standard rubric. The sources validate competency-based, multi-dimensional assessment, not the exact count of five.

agentReview.summary: Read the complete article, text-indexed all 214 deck pages and inspected the full ML-design and behavioral-leadership neighborhoods, then checked official Amazon Applied Scientist guidance, U.S. OPM structured-interview guidance, and a peer-reviewed review before choosing an original semantic reclassification visual.

implementation.accessibility: The figure has a linked learning question and a labelled list of five semantic cards. Each signal, the rounds where it can surface, and its preparation drill are written explicitly; ordinal numbers, headings, and text grouping carry all meaning without color. The established two-column primitive collapses to one column below 640 pixels, with native wrapping text and no minimum width, so it remains readable at 390 CSS pixels. Existing theme tokens provide dark-mode contrast, while shared print tokens provide a light high-contrast palette and avoid splitting the figure across pages.
